title: A check's signal must match its finding
statement: Count a fault as caught only when its own check flags the right place, never on a crash or failing run, and fail runs printing failures, whatever their exit code.
example: A validator for a generated question pool printed hard failures while exiting zero, so neither its '71/71 complete' nor exit code zero could admit the pool.
detail: A lesson project's test harness for its content checkers counts a planted fault as caught only when the checker flags the node the test case names; a flag anywhere else is a guess. A dry run of the harness showed that an uncaught exception exits the same way as a finding, so a checker that threw on every input would pass every fault case, and the harness now treats a printed stack trace as a crash whatever the exit code. Separately, a validator for a generated question pool printed hard failures while exiting zero, so its completion count and its exit code were ruled out as an admission test.
against: Exclusivity is the wrong bar for wide changes: "Wide-reaching mutations (removing an idempotency guard, reverting to the unpatched player) legitimately trip many assertions and exclusivity is the wrong bar for them" (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md`, lines 513-515).

evidence.quote: A checker that exits 1 but points at the wrong node has not found the defect, it has guessed.
An UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION also exits 1 — indistinguishable from "found a defect" by exit code alone, so a checker that throws on every input would pass every positive case.
Node prints a stack trace to stderr, which no finding ever does; treat that as a crash regardless of exit code. Found by dry-running this template, not by reasoning about it.
The validator also prints hard tell failures while exiting zero. Therefore neither “71/71 complete” nor exit code zero is an admission test.
A negative control must check that the mutation was caught BY THE NAMED ASSERTION, not merely that
A mutation caught by two assertions establishes that neither is load-bearing
WHERE you sample a state is part of the assertion
